neighbours.label: word that introduces a goal, right or purpose (to ensure, right to, strive for, attainment of)
fire: The new law protects every worker's right to fair pay and safe conditions.
We updated our procedures to ensure that every patient is seen on time.
The charity's mission is the attainment of clean water for every village.
Students who plan early set themselves up for success in their final year.
The whole team keeps striving for excellence in every product we make.
Citizens demanded the freedom to assemble and the right to vote.
The program aims at achieving lasting peace between the two regions.
Good habits help children grow and thrive in a supportive environment.
quiet: The new law covers every worker in the factory on the east side of town.
We updated our procedures and sent a copy to every patient by mail.
The charity's office is at the end of the road beside the village well.
Students who plan early put their books on the shelf for the final year.
The whole team walked to the cafeteria for lunch after the meeting.
Citizens gathered at the square and walked to the town hall.
The program starts at nine and ends at noon in the main hall.
Good habits are listed on a poster in the corner of the classroom.

notes: card: ' to' x8, ' for' x7, ' of' x5, ' achieve'/' achieving', ' ensure' in goal and rights contexts (right to privacy, set yourself up for success, attainment of goods). Probe: 'right to privacy' 0.30, 'to ensure' 0.16, 'walked to the store' 0.00. Near misses use the same prepositions with a plain spatial or part sense.
